subject: SSO scalability, SCIM provisioning & IP cordon — onboarding sequencing
messages:
From: Tim Howard <tim.howard@finova.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@finova.com
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SSO scalability, SCIM provisioning & IP allowlist — kickoff

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for making time. Quick context: we’re kicking off our Redwood pilot this month and security flagged three blockers they want explicit sequencing on before we flip auth in prod:

- SSO/SAML load testing & IdP metadata rotation behavior
- SCIM provisioning scope (groups we want mirrored) + deprovision timing
- IP allowlist strategy across our staging/production CIDR ranges (we have a VPN that will span multiple AZs)

Can you share a concrete runbook / timeline that shows order-of-ops and who owns each step? We also need a naming convention for the service accounts Redwood will create for SCIM and service-to-service keys.

Appreciate if we can get a draft by EOD Monday.

—Tim
Head of Infrastructure, Finova
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tim Howard <tim.howard@finova.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SSO scalability, SCIM provisioning & IP allowlist — kickoff

Tim — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an initial sequencing proposal below. I’ll leave internal owners copied (Marissa for config verification, Monica for SCIM scoping).

High-level sequencing (recommended):
1) Staging SSO smoke + IdP metadata rotation test (owner: Marissa) — confirm SAML metadata refresh path and expected downtime window.
2) SCIM scope & naming (owner: Monica) — export target groups, map to Redwood roles, agree on deprovision delay (default 24h).
3) Service-account creation & least-privilege policy (owner: Karthik) — agree on SA naming convention and key rotation cadence.
4) IP allowlist cordon — establish staging CIDR first, then prod; validate cross-AZ VPN egress IPs (owner: Finova security + Redwood ops).
5) End-to-end smoke + scale run (parallel) — run token-heavy generation tests to validate latency under expected concurrency.

Deliverables I’ll share by EOD Monday: MAP spreadsheet, proposed SA-naming document, and a staging cutover checklist. Attaching a technical MAP stub for reference.

Attachments: finova-map-v1.xlsx (MAP stub)

Next steps: can you confirm staging CIDR blocks and the IdP vendor (Okta / Azure AD / Ping)? Also, any readout from your security team on acceptable deprovision window?

Thanks — Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Finova sequencing + ownership (please review)

Team — forwarding Tim’s ask and the draft sequencing I just sent. Key points we need to lock before the customer deadline Monday EOD:

- Marissa: SSO rotation path + a small load test plan (10k auths over 30m) — can you outline test harness and expected metrics?
- Monica: SCIM group mapping doc and deprovision SLA — Finova prefers 24h but security might want 72h for certain groups. Please call out groups that can be immediate vs delayed.
- Ben: Service-account naming and KMS/HSM integration checklist — I sketched a policy but need your eyes on least-privilege permissions and the rotation cadence. Attached a short draft SA naming file (sa-naming-convention.md).

Risk notes: Finova’s VPN uses dynamic egress IPs across two AZs; IP allowlist will need a CIDR-based approach + possibly a small NAT gateway with static egress for prod. If they cannot provide static IPs we should propose a short-lived token fallback.

Can everyone reply with ownership + ETA by 2pm today so I can consolidate for Tim?

—Karthik
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tim Howard <tim.howard@finova.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-08T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SSO scalability, SCIM provisioning & IP allowlist — kickoff

Tim — thanks, quick answers inline and an action item table below.

SCIM scope: we recommend mirroring these groups initially: engineers, infra-admins, support, data-ops. Non-prod groups (sandbox) will be excluded initially. Deprovisioning: default 24h for engineers/support; 72h for infra-admins pending approval.

Service accounts: we propose the naming convention finova-sa-<env>-<purpose>-<short-hash>. Keys will be rotated every 90 days; we can integrate with your KMS if you provide IAM role access.

IP allowlist plan: Agree to start with staging CIDRs (10.20.0.0/16) then a planned prod cut with static NAT egress. If static egress cannot be provisioned in time, we will enable token-scoped short-lived API keys (48h) for the cutover window.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Marissa: SSO rotation test plan + harness (ETA: 6/11 EOD)
- Monica: SCIM groups mapping doc + deprovision SLA proposal (ETA: 6/10 noon) [attached: sa-naming-convention.md]
- Karthik: SA permission matrix & cutover playbook (ETA: 6/11 EOD)
- Tim/Finova security: confirm staging CIDRs + IdP vendor (ETA: 6/09 4pm)

I’ll slot time for a 30m joint run-through on Tuesday once we have the CIDRs.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tim Howard <tim.howard@finova.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: security@finova.com
Date: 2028-06-09T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SSO scalability, SCIM provisioning & IP allowlist — kickoff

Thanks all — confirming:
- IdP: Okta (metadata endpoint: https://okta.finova.com/.well-known/saml-configuration)
- Staging CIDR: 10.20.0.0/16 (confirmed)
- Deprovisioning: Ok with 24h for engineers/support; 72h for admin groups (we’ll add a sign-off later)

We’ll be available for the Tuesday run-through. I’ll ask security to check the NAT/static egress feasibility and follow up by EOD tomorrow.

—Tim
Head of Infrastructure, Finova
